same_page_reward.observed: A callback present after close, removed by B request; late A clears watchdog but hint remains 0; B only raises hint to 1.

revive_reentry.observed: Main and daily: one authoritative revive attempt, two presentation/statistic increments when B reward arrives inside A successful commit.

decisions: Keep all unresolved show IDs within one valid tool-page generation. Cancel on new generation, hide or destroy; visual occlusion alone does not cancel an earned tool.
A revive is one failed attempt, not an accumulating inventory reward. Duplicate receipts publish no second presentation/statistic; a second valid reward may still retry a failed first commit.
Reward-consumer cleanup does not remove unrelated ad_closed observers. The cached daily page still excludes ad viewing time after reopening.
Keep the existing registration/start interface and native bridge contract. Interface consolidation is optional; the reproduced defect was cancellation scope, not a need for another ad service.
Rename selection input/recipe/output meanings; preserve persisted field names and selection behavior. Keep independent historical expectations rather than permanently copying the old algorithm.

prior_verification_not_rerun.scope: Prior independent no-Autoload UI/business projects, Python tooling, simulated release, signed HTTP/PCK/Spine delivery and 22 publication cases were not rerun in this pass. The corresponding framework/transport/tooling files are unchanged; the current full product suite includes content validation, UI, business, debug boundaries and startup.

limits: Native bridge implementation is external; legacy placement-only rewarded bridges remain unavailable pending per-show signal adaptation.
Unpersisted reward events do not survive process death during persistent storage failure; ended page-specific entitlements keep their existing lifecycle rules.
Golden RNG expectations are recorded against Godot 4.6.1; an engine RNG upgrade requires explicit compatibility review.
Mobile export, actual touch/background behavior, native SDK, production CDN/TLS and visual acceptance remain external verification tasks.
Shutdown resource warnings remain recorded separately; successful scripted checks are not exhaustive timing or leak proof.
